_about: Published bread bakes with measured centre temperature, used to fit and check BakeLab. 'role' says whether a case was used for fitting ('fit') or kept unseen for checking ('holdout'). Measured values are as stated in the papers' text; no curves were digitised. 'bakelab_inputs' is our translation of each setup into BakeLab's 1D symmetric slab and is itself an approximation.

source.citation: Papasidero D., Manenti F., Pierucci S. Bread baking modeling: Coupling heat transfer and weight loss by the introduction of an explicit vaporization term. Journal of Food Engineering (accepted 21 Sept 2014, online 30 Sept 2014).

setup.shape: Italian pagnotta, roughly oblate ellipsoid, 21.7 cm diameter x 5.0 cm high, on a grid with baking paper (no pan)
setup.oven: domestic oven, 200 C setpoint, forced convection ~2 m/s, preheated; door opening dropped air to ~100 C before recovery

source.citation: Zhang L., Yang W., Xu K., Long L., Ye H. Study on Moisture Phase Changes in Bread Baking Using a Coupling Model. Foods 14 (2025) 1649. CC BY 4.0.

setup.recipe: wheat flour, water (W/F 0.55), yeast 1 g per 100 g flour; no salt mentioned
setup.dough: initial moisture 0.82 kg/kg dry basis, 64.5 g liquid water, density 1069 kg/m3, 28 C
setup.shape: ~20 mm deep layer in a 100 mm inner-diameter borosilicate glass cylinder; rose to ~51 mm on the axis
setup.probes: T1 (0, 5 mm), T2 (0, 10 mm), T3 (25, 15 mm); read as (radius, height)

bakelab_inputs._note: Amounts chosen to reproduce the stated 64.5 g water and 0.82 dry-basis moisture with BakeLab's flour composition; this implies W/F ~0.61 rather than the stated 0.55. The real layer is heated mainly from below through glass and from above, not symmetrically.
